slots.name: adult satisfaction
slots.sentence: Just 32% of American adults say they are “completely” or “somewhat” satisfied with the U.S. school system, according to an August poll published Tuesday by Gallup and the Walton Family Foundation and shared exclusively with The Associated Press. That’s an 11-point drop over the past two years and the lowest since Gallup began polling on the subject 27 years ago.

slots.name: adult dissatisfaction
slots.sentence: At the same time, dissatisfaction has increased to a high of 67%.

slots.name: parent satisfaction
slots.sentence: About two-thirds of parents with school-age children say they are satisfied with their child’s education, which is also a low point in the trend — parents haven’t had a similarly discontented view since 2013 — but double the 32% satisfaction with U.S. education among adults overall.

slots.name: Democratic satisfaction decline
slots.sentence: Democrats are driving the recent slide, with their satisfaction dropping about 19 points since President Donald Trump’s second term began in 2025.

slots.name: independent satisfaction decline
slots.sentence: Independents’ satisfaction appears to be down as well, about 10 points from 2024, while Republicans’ satisfaction has also fallen slightly, about 6 points.
